metadata.description: Delivery route accessibility filters for gene therapy targeting. AAV tropism defines POTENTIAL targets; delivery route FILTERS to ACTUAL targets.
metadata.methodology: Double-blind LLM query methodology - subagent with no therapy/disease context answered accessibility questions
metadata.key_insight: A serotype may have tropism for a cell type, but if the delivery route cannot physically access that cell type, transduction will not occur.

Hepatocytes.notes: Primary target for IV AAV delivery. Fenestrated endothelium allows direct access. Liver acts as dominant 'sink' for most AAV serotypes.

Skeletal_muscle_cells.notes: Dose-dependent transduction. Good access for muscle-tropic serotypes (AAVrh74, AAV9).

Satellite_cells.notes: Muscle satellite cells accessible but only dividing cells well-transduced

Cardiomyocytes.notes: Good cardiac access for AAV9, AAVrh74. Heart among most efficiently transduced organs after liver.

Excitatory_neurons.notes: CNS neurons accessible only with BBB-crossing serotypes (AAV9) and age-dependent. Neonates: yes. Adults: limited.

Inhibitory_neurons.notes: Same BBB constraints as excitatory neurons

Limbic_system_neurons.notes: Deep brain structures poorly accessed via IV even with BBB-crossing serotypes

Purkinje_neurons.notes: AAV9 IV can reach Purkinje cells in cerebellum, but efficiency lower than direct injection

Granule_neurons.notes: Cerebellar granule neurons accessible via IV AAV9 but with lower efficiency

Astrocytes.notes: AAV9 preferentially transduces astrocytes in ADULTS (neuronal preference in neonates)

Oligodendrocytes.notes: Some oligodendrocyte transduction with AAV9 IV, less efficient than neurons/astrocytes

Microglia.notes: Microglia are very difficult to transduce with any AAV serotype. Use ex vivo HSC approaches for microglia-targeted therapy.

Photoreceptor_cells.notes: Blood-retinal barrier blocks IV access to retina. Requires subretinal or intravitreal injection.

Retinal_pigment_cells.notes: Blood-retinal barrier blocks IV access. Requires subretinal injection.

Hematopoietic_stem_cells.notes: HSCs poorly transduced by AAV. Use ex vivo lentiviral transduction.

Adult_CB_CD34+.notes: CD34+ cells poorly transduced by AAV. Use ex vivo approaches.

Thymocytes.notes: Immune cells poorly transduced by AAV

Adult_T_cell.notes: T cells poorly transduced by AAV. Use lentivirus or retrovirus for CAR-T.

Erythroblasts.notes: Erythroid cells poorly transduced by AAV

neonatal.description: BBB more permeable in neonates; better CNS access
neonatal.therapeutic_window: Zolgensma approved for <2 years; optimal CNS transduction in infants

adult.description: Mature BBB significantly limits CNS access
adult.note: AAV9 IV in adults preferentially transduces astrocytes over neurons

AAV9.description: AAV9 crosses BBB, especially efficiently in neonates. The only AAV serotype with well-documented CNS penetration after IV delivery.
AAV9.notes: BBB crossing efficiency is age-dependent: neonates > infants > adults. In adults, astrocytes are preferentially transduced over neurons.

AAV-PHP.eB.description: Engineered AAV9 variant with enhanced BBB crossing in mice. Note: BBB crossing NOT validated in humans or NHPs.
AAV-PHP.eB.notes: PHP.eB relies on LY6A receptor which is absent in primates. Do not assume human translatability.

AAVrh10.description: Some CNS penetration reported but less efficient than AAV9.

AAV5.description: Primarily liver-tropic. Minimal CNS penetration after IV delivery.

AAV8.description: Primarily liver-tropic. Minimal CNS penetration after IV delivery.

AAVrh74.description: Muscle-tropic serotype. Does NOT cross BBB.

AAV1.description: Muscle-tropic serotype. Does NOT cross BBB.

Excitatory_neurons.notes: Excellent transduction at injection site (2-5mm radius). Can spread via axonal transport to connected regions.

Limbic_system_neurons.notes: Direct injection to putamen/striatum efficiently transduces limbic neurons (used for Upstaza/Kebilidi)

Purkinje_neurons.notes: Cerebellar injection can target Purkinje neurons

Astrocytes.notes: Astrocytes at injection site transduced, though less efficiently than neurons for most serotypes

Oligodendrocytes.notes: Oligodendrocytes at injection site can be transduced

Microglia.notes: Microglia very difficult to transduce even with direct injection. Use ex vivo HSC approaches.

Hepatocytes.notes: Compartmentalized - no systemic spread from brain injection

AFP_ALB_positive_cells.notes: No liver access from intracranial route

Photoreceptor_cells.notes: Retina not accessible from brain injection

Retinal_pigment_cells.notes: Retina not accessible from brain injection

spread_characteristics.axonal_transport: Can spread to connected brain regions via anterograde/retrograde transport

serotype_differences.AAV2: Limited spread due to heparan sulfate binding; highly localized
serotype_differences.AAV9: Better spread than AAV2; broader neuronal transduction

intrathecal.description: Injection into cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) via lumbar puncture

Excitatory_neurons.notes: Surface/superficial neurons accessible. Deep brain parenchyma poorly reached.

Limbic_system_neurons.notes: Deep basal ganglia structures poorly accessed via IT

DRG_neurons.notes: Dorsal root ganglia neurons excellently accessed via IT. However, this is a SAFETY CONCERN (DRG toxicity observed).

Ependymal_cells.notes: Ependymal cells lining ventricles and central canal directly exposed to CSF

Hepatocytes.notes: CSF is compartmentalized from systemic circulation

spinal_cord_access.notes: Spinal cord surface structures well accessed; good for SMA-type applications

Ependymal_cells.notes: Primary target - cells lining the ventricles directly exposed

Excitatory_neurons.notes: Periventricular neurons accessible; deep cortex poorly reached

Choroid_plexus.notes: Choroid plexus directly exposed to ventricular CSF

subretinal.description: Injection beneath the retina, between RPE and photoreceptors

Retinal_pigment_cells.notes: PRIMARY TARGET - RPE cells directly contacted by subretinal injection. Gold standard for RPE-targeted therapy (Luxturna).

Photoreceptor_cells.notes: Photoreceptor outer segments directly contact injection site. Well transduced for both rods and cones.

Bipolar_cells.notes: Inner nuclear layer less accessible than outer retina

Retinal_ganglion_cells.notes: Inner retina/ganglion cell layer NOT accessible from subretinal space. Use intravitreal for RGCs.

Excitatory_neurons.notes: CNS neurons not accessible from retinal injection

coverage_notes.bleb_formation: Creates a retinal detachment bleb; transduction limited to bleb area
coverage_notes.bilateral_treatment: Requires separate injection for each eye
coverage_notes.surgical_risk: Requires vitrectomy; more invasive than intravitreal

intravitreal.description: Injection into vitreous humor of the eye

Retinal_ganglion_cells.notes: PRIMARY TARGET for intravitreal. Ganglion cell layer most accessible from vitreous.

Muller_glia.notes: Muller cell bodies span retina; endfeet accessible from vitreous

Photoreceptor_cells.notes: Outer retina NOT accessible from vitreous. ILM and retinal layers block penetration. Use subretinal for photoreceptors.

Retinal_pigment_cells.notes: RPE at opposite side of retina from vitreous. Not accessible. Use subretinal.

advantages.repeatable: Can be repeated more easily than subretinal

Skeletal_muscle_cells.notes: Primary target - myofibers at injection site efficiently transduced

Satellite_cells.notes: Muscle satellite cells partially accessible; only dividing cells well transduced

Excitatory_neurons.notes: Motor neurons can be reached via RETROGRADE AXONAL TRANSPORT only

Cardiomyocytes.notes: Different compartment - cardiac muscle not accessible from skeletal muscle injection

Hepatocytes.notes: Minimal systemic spread from IM injection

spread_characteristics.local_only: Transduction largely confined to injection site muscle group
spread_characteristics.retrograde_transport: Some motor neuron transduction via retrograde axonal transport

HSCT.description: Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (ex vivo gene therapy)

Hematopoietic_stem_cells.notes: Primary target for ex vivo transduction. Cells are collected, transduced ex vivo with lentivirus, then re-infused.

Adult_CB_CD34+.notes: CD34+ cells isolated and transduced ex vivo

Microglia.notes: Microglia are derived from engrafted HSCs. This is how Skysona/Lenmeldy/Libmeldy deliver enzyme to CNS.

Thymocytes.notes: T cell progenitors derived from engrafted HSCs

Erythroblasts.notes: Erythroid cells derived from engrafted HSCs (Casgevy, Lyfgenia for SCD)

Hepatocytes.notes: Liver cells not derived from HSCs

mechanism_notes.cns_delivery: HSC-derived microglia migrate to brain and can deliver therapeutic enzymes to CNS (used for CALD, MLD)
mechanism_notes.conditioning: Requires chemotherapy conditioning to create 'space' for engraftment
mechanism_notes.durability: Engrafted cells are self-renewing - potentially lifelong correction

effective_tropism_calculation.description: Effective tropism = Serotype tropism AND Route accessibility
effective_tropism_calculation.formula: For each cell type: if serotype_tropism[cell] >= threshold AND route_access[cell] in ['yes', 'limited'], then cell is effectively targetable

exact.description: Pipeline predicts the same cell type as therapy target

aav_reachable.description: Different prediction, but predicted cell is in AAV tropism range AND accessible via delivery route

route_unreachable.description: AAV has tropism for predicted cell, BUT delivery route cannot access it
route_unreachable.example: If AAVrh74 IV predicts CNS neurons - AAVrh74 has minimal CNS tropism AND IV doesn't help

related.description: Same tissue system (e.g., both CNS neurons) but different specific cell type

different.description: Prediction is different tissue/system from target
